messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] ANOVA loop
parts:
Say y is a phenotype of length n and X is a matrix of genotypes of dimension n x p.

pval <- apply(X, 2, function(gen,phe)
anova(aov(phe ~ gen))[1,5], y)

You may need to use as.factor(gen), as follows:

pval <- apply(X, 2, function(gen,phe)
anova(aov(phe ~ as.factor(gen)))[1,5], y)

As a for loop:

pval <- rep(NA, ncol(X))
for(i in 1:ncol(gen))
pval[i] <- anova(aov(y ~ as.factor(X[,i])))[1,5]

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] ANOVA loop
parts:
Hello all,
I recently did this to do a pairwise epistasis test using ANOVA.   I wrote several functions that handled it.  I can't promise that they are the most efficient way, and Karl's way is likely more appropriate, but I will send them along anyhow so that they might be helpful to others.

You will call pairwiseMarkerAnovas and then getPairwiseAnovaDF if you wand a simplified data.frame as your output.

### Epistasis tests
# twoMarkerAOV(cross, chr)
# getInteractionP(x)
# generatePairwiseMarkerList(cross, verbose)
# pairwiseMarkerANOVAs(cross, pheno.col, verbose)
# getPairwiseAnovaDF(x)
#


#####
# twoMarkerAOV(cross, chr)
# Calculates an ANOVA for the effect of a markerpair on a phenotype column.
# returns a list with three elements (Marker Name1, Marker Name2, AOV results)
#####

twoMarkerAOV <- function(cross=NULL, pheno.col=NULL, mname1=NULL, mname2=NULL, verbose=FALSE) {
  if (verbose>1) {cat("marker1:",mname1,"marker2:",mname2,"\n")}
  if ((mname1 %in% markernames(cross)) & (mname2 %in% markernames(cross))) {
    pos <- find.markerpos(cross, c(mname1, mname2))
    m1 <- pull.geno(cross,pos$chr[1])[,mname1,drop=FALSE]
    m2 <- pull.geno(cross,pos$chr[2])[,mname2,drop=FALSE]
    return(list(mname1=mname1,mname2=mname2,aov_results=summary(aov(cross$pheno[,pheno.col] ~ m1 * m2))[[1]]))
  }
}

#####
# getInteractionP(x)
# getMarker1(x)
# getMarker2(x)
# takes the results from twoMarkerAOV and retuns the interaction P value or the
# names of the marker Best used as
# part of an apply call to the list generated by pairwiseMarkerANOVA
#####

getInteractionP <- function(x) {
  x$aov_results$"Pr(>F)"[3]
}

getMarker1P <- function(x) {
  x$aov_results$"Pr(>F)"[1]
}
getMarker2P <- function(x) {
  x$aov_results$"Pr(>F)"[2]
}


getMarker1 <- function(x) {
  x$mname1
}

getMarker2 <- function(x) {
  x$mname2
}

#####
# generatePairwiseMarkerList(cross, verbose)
# takes a cross object and returns a dataframe with two columns representing each
# unique marker pair.  The second marker cycles within the first marker.
#####

generatePairwiseMarkerList <- function(cross, verbose=FALSE) {
  m <- markernames(cross)
  m1 <-NULL
  m2 <-NULL
  numMarker <- totmar(cross)
  for (i in 1:(numMarker-1)) {
    for (j in (i+1):numMarker) {
      m1 <- rbind(m1,m[i])
      m2 <- rbind(m2,m[j])
    } # for j in i+1:numMa7rker
  } # for i in 1:numMarker
  if (verbose) {cat("Generated Pairwise Marker List with",length(m1),"marker pairs.\n\n")}
  return(markerlist<-as.data.frame(cbind(m1,m2)))
}


#####
# pairwiseMarkerANOVAs(cross, pheno.col, verbose)
# generates ANOVA results for all marker pairs in a cross object.  Returns a list where
# each element represents the test for a single marker pair and includes three elements
# the two marker names and the output from aov.
#####

pairwiseMarkerANOVAs <- function(cross, pheno.col=1, verbose=FALSE) {
  markerlist <- generatePairwiseMarkerList(cross,verbose)
  if(verbose) {cat("Beginning Pairwse ANOVAs...")}
  return(apply(markerlist, MARGIN=1, function(x) twoMarkerAOV(cross,pheno.col,as.character(x[1]),
                                                          as.character(x[2]),verbose)))
}

#####
# getPairwiseAnovaDF(x)
# Takes list output from pairwiseMarkerANOVAs and outputs a usable dataframe.
#####

getPairwiseAnovaDF <- function(y) {
  interaction.p <- sapply(y, function(x) getInteractionP(x))
  mname1 <- sapply(y, function(x) getMarker1(x))
  mname2 <- sapply(y, function(x) getMarker2(x))
  m1.p <- sapply(y, function(x) getMarker1P(x))
  m2.p <- sapply(y, function(x) getMarker2P(x))
  df <- data.frame(mname1=mname1, mname2=mname2,
                          m1.p=m1.p, m2.p=m2.p,
                          interaction.p=interaction.p)
}
